title: Handoff Receipts — durable close-out proof
text: self_score predecessor_score distinct keys one can never stand ; omit predecessor_score Session 1 (predecessor score). commit: pending what_was_done: pending legal write time (receipt ships commit whose sha name); next session reconciles real shas.
code: ```handoff session: S<N> date: YYYY-MM-DD status: <pending | complete> self_score: <1-10> predecessor_score: <1-10> active_task: <current state> what_was_done: <what you did, including a commit sha — or the literal `pending`> next_steps: <specific and actionable; never "pick next from backlog"> key_files: <each entry carries a path:line token, e.g. SessionManager.java:245> gotchas: <traps the next session should watch for> runtime_smoke: <a run result, or "n/a — docs-only", or "impossible: <reason>"> changelog_ref: <PR #N or a short-sha into CHANGELOG.md> commit: <short-sha — or `pending` until the next session reconciles it> ``` <free-text prose: the durable proxy for the Phase 3G spoken report, plus the +/- self-score breakdown>  Write clean `key: value` lines — no inline `#` comments (a `#` is a literal value character, as in `changelog_ref: PR #52`). The keys are the six Phase 3D Minimum Handoff Requirements (the sixth *is* `self_score`) plus `predecessor_score` (the Phase 3A evaluation) and a little metadata. `status` is `pending` at the Phase 1B claim and `complete` at close-out; a third value, `reconciled`, is written *only* by a later session's Phase 0 reconcile when it reconstructs a receipt a crashed session never completed — you never write it yourself.

title: PED + GV Cluster Audit (Session 2)

Broadened 7 <NAME>.*\.md$ (.Rbuildignore:77-84): PROJECT_LEARNINGS, CLAUDE, SESSION_RUNNER, SAFEGUARDS, BACKLOG, ROADMAP, CHANGELOG. dupe (CLAUDE 2.md, CHANGELOG copy.md) otherwise re-raised exact WARNING S58 just killed SESSION_NOTES. Killing class means covering every member, one bit last. (b) [Rbuildignore-lines---regexes] load-bearing new fact: .Rbuildignore comment syntax — every line perl regex matched relative paths. existing #-prefixed “comments” work happens VALID regex matches real file (path containing literal comment text doesn’t exist). added multi-line # comment whose 2nd/3rd lines held unbalanced ( (... sync dupes ( 2.md,) → R CMD build aborted immediately: Error ... invalid regular expression '# Patterns broadened ...('. fix: keep every comment line valid regex — balanced parens , safest, parens / leading quantifier (*,+,?). left inline NOTE file warning next editor. TELL regex-file, prose-file: line 73’s original (tooling, R package content) works parens balanced. (c) [build step test] caught build-level verify (Learning 58b), eye — static read comment looked fine. .Rbuildignore edit’s authoritative gate R CMD build; running EVERY edit (just pattern lines) surfaced invalid-regex abort ship. (d) [zsh--bash: word-split unquoted scalars] Bash tool runs zsh, n $NAMES split unquoted scalar whitespace (bash ). first verify loop iterated whole string → created 1 bogus file named PROJECT_LEARNINGS CLAUDE ... 2.md instead 7. Use explicit literal list (n B C ...) real array, never unquoted space-joined scalar, loop’s correctness depends word-splitting. (e) [authoritative build proof] Staged 14 REAL spaced dupes (2.md copy.md forms × 7 names) → R CMD build (RC=0) → tar tzf (693 files) → ZERO 7 names .md (dupes canonicals excluded), real content (DESCRIPTION/NAMESPACE) present; trap cleanup EXIT removed dupes + tarball. Paired -7-names regex probe (RED-equivalent): OLD misses every dupe form, NEW catches 2.md/copy.md -match <NAME>.Rmd/<NAME>_archive.txt. (f) [scope--decision---owner] Two genuine author-decisions posed via AskUserQuestion editing: pattern style (loose .* match S58’s shipped line — chosen — vs targeted ( [0-9]+| copy)? zero -match) file scope (already-ignored cluster — chosen, pure behavior-none — vs ALSO adding currently-UNignored docs like RECOMMENDED_SKILLS.md/audit files, change tarball contents + shrink top-level-files NOTE, DIFFERENT change). Deferring latter kept pure dupe-guard. Reflexes: [verify-first][build--check][macos-dupe-scan][news-vs-changelog][declare-N/-honestly][right-sized-orchestration][commit--scope-switch]. what: Learning 60 — Execute the deferred scope-B: exclude ALL non-shipping top-level files to eliminate the “non-standard top-level files” NOTE — and BUILD THE BASELINE TARBALL to enumerate the real set, don’t trust the handoff’s candidate list (S60, repo hygiene / .Rbuildignore)
title: nprcgenekeepr — Project-Specific Learnings
text: () [enumerate---artifact, handoff] handoff’s candidate-file list incomplete; authoritative set came building baseline tarball. S59’s SUGGESTED-NEXT #1 named 4 candidate files (RECOMMENDED_SKILLS.md, TECH_DEBT_AUDIT, PED_GV_AUDIT.{md,html}) actual NOTE comprised 8 — also 20250504_cran-comments.md, methodology_dashboard.py, dashboard.html, nprcgenekeepr_notes.txt. got complete set R CMD build → tar tzf <tarball> | grep -E '^pkg/[^/]+$' (tarball’s top-level FILES exactly NOTE’s input), subtracting 5 standard files (DESCRIPTION/NAMESPACE/NEWS.md/README.md/LICENSE). Lesson: “shrink/eliminate NOTE” task, enumerate built artifact, prose candidate list — pose scope AskUserQuestion real set, options grounded reality. (b) [NOTE pure function tarball top-level contents] “Non-standard files/directories found top level” computed R CMD check unpacked tarball’s top-level entries minus fixed standard set, building + listing top-level entries AUTHORITATIVE gate — full devtools::check() needed (build--check logic Learning 58b, applied NOTE rather WARNING). Excluding 8 left exactly 5 standard files (685 files vs 693 baseline = 8 removed) → NOTE eliminated, verified directly. (c) [consolidate--prevent-recurrence] root cause 20250504_cran-comments.md shipping 7 sibling exact-match lines + missed 8th. Replaced 7 dated ^YYYYMMDD_cran-comments\.md$ one ^[0-9]+_cran-comments\.md$ — NEW dated cran-comments file now auto-ignored, killing “someone adds dated file forgets ignore line” class. find N exact-match lines dated/numbered family, single regex durable fix. (d) [dupe-guard dupes happen] Used <NAME>.* (dupe-guarded) macOS-synced methodology/audit docs (RECOMMENDED_SKILLS, PED_GV_AUDIT, TECH_DEBT_AUDIT) tight ^X\.ext$ methodology_dashboard.py/dashboard.html/nprcgenekeepr_notes.txt cran-comments regex — aren’t sync-prone, broad form add -match risk benefit. Match guard actual threat, don’t apply .* reflexively. (e) [zsh-nomatch ABORTS, cont. 59d] rm -f nprcgenekeepr_*.tar.gz matching file ABORTED whole script zsh (matches found) R CMD build ran — even -f, zsh errors unmatched glob unless unsetopt nomatch / setopt null_glob. ’d applied zsh lesson dupe-staging array forgot cleanup glob; prefix unsetopt nomatch 2>/dev/null; setopt null_glob 2>/dev/null glob might match. Reflexes: [verify-first][build--check][macos-dupe-scan][news-vs-changelog][declare-N/-honestly][right-sized-orchestration][commit--scope-switch]. Apply: “shrink/eliminate top-level-files NOTE,” build baseline tarball enumerate real non-standard set, exclude per owner scope, re-build confirm top level standard files; consolidate dated/numbered families one regex; disable zsh nomatch glob cleanups.

what: Learning 61 — Closing a STALE issue (resolved by a prior session but never formally closed): verify the integration is LIVE and PINNED firsthand before closing — the proof is a test that would FAIL if reverted to the placeholder (S61, issue #34 close)
title: nprcgenekeepr — Project-Specific Learnings
text: () [verify--gating-fact-firsthand, cont. 57a] deliverable closing issue, gating fact issue’s resolution CLAIM — establish firsthand, don’t infer “looks done.” #34 (“integrate qcStudbook modInput”, bug/high) described placeholder QC (# TODO: Replace actual qcStudbook() call + results$cleaned <- rawData); current modInput.R:408/423 already calls qcStudbook()/runQcStudbook(). integration landed Shiny-module conversion (commit 7da01afe, extended c9019d51/bb7f2be6) CHANGELOG.md’s Session-20 entry (:1216-1217) even recorded “#34 … stale (already integrated)” — yet nobody closed GitHub issue. issue can outlive resolution; closing evidence-gated deliverable. handoff chain (S20→S60) kept listing #34 “highest-value open BUG implement” CHANGELOG already knew done — systemic issue-tracker-lags-code gap, one session’s miss. (b) [pin-test = integration proof; [mutation-check] sibling] single strongest evidence claimed-complete integration REAL test FAIL code reverted placeholder. test_modInput_qcStudbook.R:296 asserts "gen" %% names(cleaned); gen added qcStudbook() (qcStudbook.R:267), never old results$cleaned <- rawData passthrough → one assertion pins live path. verifying “X actually wired,” don’t just confirm call exists — locate (note ABSENCE ) discriminating test placeholder failed. (c) [firsthand test gate — skips load-bearing] test_qcStudbook.R 38/0/0/0 + test_modInput_qcStudbook.R 90/0/0/0 (pass/fail/err/skip). 0 skips mattered: shiny::testServer module-server tests carry skip_if_not_installed("shiny"), nonzero skip mean end--end module path never executed green hollow. Confirm shiny installed → tests actually drove modInputServer (upload → getData → assert cleaned studbook). (d) [right-sized adversarial close ultracode] irreversible public act HIGH-priority bug, ran small 3-lens refute--close workflow (residual-placeholder/live-path ‖ functional-completeness-vs-issue-intent ‖ test-authenticity), skeptic told find reason close → refuted=false, high confidence, 0 gaps. AUTHORITATIVE test gate run parent firsthand, trusted agents (agents read code; ran R). 3-lens fan-proportionate ; heavier pass ceremony, solo close underuse ultracode budget. (First launch failed unsupported run_in_background arg — Workflow always backgrounds; re-invoked clean, one self-corrected round-trip.) (e) [declare-N/-honestly, cont. 57d/58c] verify--close session writes production code tests → TDD phase N/every response; pre-committed fixing -session gap surfaced (separate TDD session) scope discipline held even “’m ” temptation. Reflexes: [verify-first][verify--gating-fact][mutation-check][right-sized-orchestration][declare-N/-honestly][news-vs-changelog][commit--scope-switch]. what: Learning 62 — Backlog-staleness audit: generalize the #34 finding to the WHOLE tracker via a classify→adversarial-refute fan-out — the refute pass earns its keep by knocking down a false-STALE the owner himself had flagged in 2020 (S62, audit / docs/audits/)
title: nprcgenekeepr — Project-Specific Learnings

(c) [verify-close-relevant-calls firsthand — incl. issue’s comments] Re-verified 3 close-relevant calls (#14/#8/#1) firsthand source GitHub. agent CITED #1 owner comment evidence; confirmed real via gh api repos/:owner/:repo/issues/1/comments (bare gh issue view 1 printed empty — TTY/pager quirk; API showed 1 comment). Agents read code; parent runs authoritative checks (: gh api, R-free grep/Read orderReport.R:44-54 + rankSubjects.R:38,43 #8, test assertions test_modInput_qcStudbook.R:538-545 #14). (d) [search--CONTENT, cited line] load-bearing classifier instruction: old issues’ line numbers drifted, grep quoted TODO TEXT / function name, never cited line. #35’s placeholder moved issue’s “lines 246-253” modPedigree.R:292-302 (real trimPedigree() call replacing ) — line-number check misses resolution; content search finds reveals ’s ancestors (getProbandPedigree walks backward ), PARTIAL STALE. (e) [hold STALE #34 bar] STALE = placeholder REPLACED real logic, TODO deleted/reworded. 14 OPEN issues still carry cited TODO VERBATIM (fillBins.R:6 “RMS provide description”, agePyramidPlot.R:60 chimp TODO, getPotentialParents.R:92-94 “bit hack”, removeAutoGenIds.R:4-6 leading-U). #8 confirmed-resolved--CAVEATED → downgraded close--NOTE (functional -solutions-live, gated optional origin column + test asserts Undetermined/rank=NA branch) — distinct #14’s clean close. Placed report docs/audits/ — build-ignored via .Rbuildignore:15 ^docs$ — regress S60’s elimination “non-standard top-level files” NOTE (top-level dated audit file like existing PED_GV_AUDIT/TECH_DEBT_AUDIT re-added ). what: Learning 63 — Executing an audit’s close recommendation is itself evidence-gated: re-verify intent-completeness firsthand (it re-graded #14 from “clean” to “caveated”), and reconcile EVERY adversarial verdict against a load_all run — a “tests failing” refutation was a stale-installed-binary artifact (S63, issue #14 close)
title: nprcgenekeepr — Project-Specific Learnings
text: () [audit’s confidence HUNCH re-verified — don’t inherit ] S62 classified #14 “clean close, high confidence”; firsthand verification re-graded close--CAVEAT. audit’s per-issue classifier checked headline (separate-genotype-file path works + test pin passes) stopped . deeper check found commonPedGenoFile (combined-file) UI mode never integer-codes string alleles → genotypes never satisfy hasGenotype() never reach geneDrop(). Lesson: verify--close session executing audit recommendation must independently re-check intent-completeness WHOLE issue (: EVERY input mode track, just one audit cited), ratify audit’s grade. audit recommending close start verification, end . Learning 61() applied recommendation rather raw backlog item. (b) [reconcile adversarial verdict firsthand evidence — refuted≠true, refuted≠false, checked] 3-lens refute pass returned 1 confirm + 2 refuted; one refutation REAL one ARTIFACT. intent-completeness refutation (combined-file caveat) real changed deliverable. test-authenticity refutation — “test :503-547 actively FAILING, installed modInputServer missing genotype merge block” — FALSE: agent decompiled stale installed binary (compiled RDB) instead source. pkgload::load_all run 90/0/0/0 read merge block R/modInput.R:384-396 directly. Lesson: subagent claims R test failing code missing, may inspecting getNamespaceVersion/installed namespace, can lag working tree; authoritative source gate load_all (fresh install) run parent. Don’t accept refuted=true face value don’t dismiss — verify verdict firsthand; value refute pass questions raises, verdicts returns. (c) [stale-install recurring R-package verification trap — version string proof currency] getNamespaceVersion("nprcgenekeepr") returns rolling dev 1.1.0.9000 whether installed binary current months stale. matching version mean installed code equals source. agent decompiling installed namespace can therefore “see” code source already superseded (, , code source ADDED install lacks). Always test via load_all working tree verifying source-level claim; never let installed-binary inspection stand . (d) [verification flipped approved premise → re-confirm owner, even something decided] combined-file caveat DELIBERATE parity choice owner’s commit c9019d51. Even , changed close “clean” framing owner approved (picking “#14” menu) caveated one, surfaced via AskUserQuestion (clean / caveated / keep-open-narrowed) rather silently downgrading unilaterally closing. owner chose caveated close. Lesson: firsthand verification flips premise approved outward-facing action, re-confirm framing — owning past design decision authorizing today’s issue-state change new understanding. (Safeguards: “find contradicts described, surface instead proceeding.”) (e) [“close caveat” authorizes close + comment, new tracker writes — classifier enforced correctly] tried file 1-line follow-enhancement combined-file gap; auto-mode classifier DENIED (approved action closing #14; new issue separate external write). Right boundary. captured residual close comment instead (file pointers future enhancement needs) labeled “filed.” Lesson: outward-facing scope approved narrowly, keep within — record spun-gaps artifact authorized write, leave issue-creation owner unless explicitly approved. Don’t treat “optionally also…” menu option standing authorization. Reflexes: [verify-first][verify--gating-fact][reconcile-agent-claims-firsthand][stale-install-trap][author-decision][right-sized-orchestration][declare-N/-honestly][news-vs-changelog][commit--scope-switch]. Apply: executing audit’s close recommendation, re-verify issue’s FULL intent firsthand (every mode/path, just cited one) — audit’s grade hunch; run refute--close pass reconcile verdict pkgload::load_all run (stale installed binary yields false “tests failing”/“code missing” refutations); verification re-grades close, re-confirm framing owner via AskUserQuestion; keep new-issue creation “close caveat” scope — document spun-gaps close comment.

what: Learning 64 — When an adversarial gate SPLITS, reconcile the dissenting verdict by REPRODUCTION, not majority vote — a “hold-open” outvoted 2-to-1 was substantively right, and reproducing its claim (optional-column gating silently recreates the original bug) upgraded a footnote caveat into a strengthened one (S64, issue #8 close)
title: nprcgenekeepr — Project-Specific Learnings
text: () [split gate decided evidence, vote count] 3-lens refute pass closing #8 returned 1 hold-open (refuted=true, high) + 2 close--caveat (refuted=false, high). tempting move go 2--3 majority. Instead reconstructed dissenter’s central claim code: -parent founder offspring, run orderReport() without origin column → value="High Value", rank=1 (exact bug #8 describes); origin (NA ONPRC-born animal) → "Undetermined"/NA. reproduction CONFIRMED hold-open verdict’s substance even though outvoted. Lesson: adversarial verdicts inputs firsthand reconciliation, poll tallied — lone dissenter exactly one reproduce, ’s right changes deliverable. (Extends Learning 63(b): reconcile verdict; 64 adds: disagree, reproduction breaks tie, count.) (b) [optional-column gating SILENTLY recreates bug stronger finding footnote caveat] S62 audit graded #8 “close CAVEAT” treating origin gating (R/orderReport.R:31 ("origin" %% names(rpt))) footnote. Firsthand, gating means fix NOTHING — warning — studbook lacking optional origin column (absent bundled datasets; origin reaches report via intersect(getIncludeColumns(), names(ped)) R/reportGV.R:119). headline symptom fully present default path. Lesson: “implemented gated optional input” automatically minor caveat — check happens DEFAULT path whether user warned; safeguard silently -ops materially worse audit’s one-line note implied. staleness classifier checks headline + cited anchors stops; won’t probe alternate input path long comment thread’s second arc (, orphaned 2021 simulated-kinship subsystem + unresolved “discuss Matt” design item). (c) [premise-flip → re-confirm--owner reflex S63, second time running] Firsthand verification flipped approved premise (audit’s footnote caveat → reproduced silent-failure + orphaned subsystem), surfaced via AskUserQuestion (close--strengthened-caveat / hold-open--re-scope / close--file-followup) irreversible gh issue close. Owner chose strengthened caveat. Held S63 scope boundary: documented three remaining items (origin-absent safeguard, regression test, simulated-kinship integration) close comment candidate enhancements filed new issues. Lesson: premise-flip reflex isn’t one-— every audit-driven close gated re-verifying intent firsthand, reproduction (just code read) strongest re-grade evidence bring owner. Reflexes: [verify-first][reproduce--dissenting-verdict][verify--gating-fact][default-path--just-headline][author-decision][surface-premise-flip][scope-discipline][declare-N/-honestly][news-vs-changelog]. Apply: adversarial refute gate splits, reproduce dissenting (hold-open) verdict’s claim code deciding — majority “close” verdicts outweigh one reproduced blocker; treat optional-input gating potential silent-failure (test default path + check warning), footnote; verification re-grades approved close, re-confirm framing owner via AskUserQuestion keep new-issue creation “close caveat” scope.

what: Learning 65 — “Update a stale inventory issue” is a recompute-from-scratch task, not a patch-the-named-clusters task: the handoff said ≈2 clusters flipped; a call-graph reachability recomputation found 45 of 70 listed functions are now used (S65, issue #37 update)

text: () [recompute, don’t patch cited clusters] S64 (inheriting S62 audit) framed #37 “strike resolved Shiny-module + genotype rows; keep still-accurate unused-export inventory” — ≈7 functions, “bulk holds.” -scratch reachability recomputation found 45 70 listed functions now used app (22 + 3 S3 methods still unused); totals 155 exports / 116 used / 39 unused vs issue’s 108 / 38 / 70. per-issue classifier checked headline (4 Shiny modules) + genotype anchor stopped — calibration miss flagged S62→#14 S63→#8, amplified #37 70-row inventory, single yes/. Lesson: deliverable “update stale inventory,” unit work recomputing WHOLE inventory, patching rows handoff names; handoff tells start, much stale. Stale entries inherited framing left place included rankSubjects, calcGU, filterKinMatrix/Report/Threshold, getOffspring, withinIntegerRange — now live. (b) [call-graph reachability right tool ’s reproducible] codetools::findGlobals(f, merge=FALSE)$functions ∩ package-functions gives function’s callees; BFS app entry seeds {runModularApp, runGeneKeepR, appUI, appServer} yields transitive “used app” set; exported names outside unused. rigorous grep (follows call graph, text matches) reliable farming per-function judgments agents (conflate test/man/@examples references app use — roxygen lives comments correctly seen findGlobals, parses function body). Concrete call paths evidence ship (e.g. rankSubjects: appServer → modGeneticValueServer → reportGV → orderReport → rankSubjects). Put method issue inventory reproducible, one-time snapshot. (c) [name static method’s blind spots CHECK — don’t hand-wave] findGlobals misses dynamic dispatch (.call/match.fun/get string calls) S3 generic dispatch. Checked explicitly: string-dispatched call R/ .call("rbind", …) (base), NONE 22 still-unused names appear string literal anywhere R/ → dynamic invocation closure missed; 3 S3 methods (print.summary.*, summary.nprcgenekeeprErr) aren’t dispatched app path (app’s summary() calls hit summary.default numeric vectors). stated--checked limitation verification; unstated one latent error. (Also note 3 S3 methods aren’t even getNamespaceExports — registered via S3method — yet issue author counted exported; keep S3 caveat rather silently dropping .) (d) [outward-facing edit, surface FORM + SCOPE acting] Editing owner’s issue body reversible (GitHub keeps edit history) still overwrites authored text, “also add 17 newer unused exports” expands scope beyond literal task. owner’s call → ONE AskUserQuestion concrete previews (strikethrough--place vs rewrite vs comment-; scope--70 vs add--17) let owner choose grounded mockups; timeline pointer comment silent body edit isn’t invisible watchers. surface--irreversible discipline S63/S64 used closes, applied UPDATE. Reflexes: [verify-first][recompute-don’t-patch][reproducible-method---artifact][name--check--blind-spot][surface-form--scope][right-sized-orchestration][declare-N/-honestly][news-vs-changelog][macos-dupe-scan]. what: Learning 67 — Re-scoping a partially-done feature issue: verify which half shipped AND validate the issue’s OWN suggested API against the code (it can cite a signature that doesn’t exist), then expose the semantic fork the one-line ask hides (S67, issue #35 re-scope)
title: nprcgenekeepr — Project-Specific Learnings
text: () [issue’s “Suggested Implementation” claim verify, spec inherit] #35 proposed trimPedigree(focalIds(), ped, ancestors = TRUE, descendants = TRUE) — trimPedigree’s real signature (probands, ped, removeUninformative = FALSE, addBackParents = FALSE); ancestors/descendants params never existed. re-scope copied issue’s suggested call forward handed implementer non-compiling spec. body ALSO cited stale placeholder lines 246-253 already replaced live ancestor logic 292-302. Lesson: grooming feature issue, check every API body names actual function definition — author-proposed code old issue ages exactly like cited line numbers . Read signature, don’t trust snippet. (b) [verify half “X Y” ask already shipped — reading call chain, title] #35 = “include ancestors descendants.” Firsthand: ancestors DONE (modPedigree.R:292-302 → trimPedigree → getProbandPedigree, upward sire/dam closure getProbandPedigree.R:24-40), descendants — neither walks downward, getOffspring single-level . Lesson: compound feature ask, re-scope’s first job partition done/-done live call graph; handoff’s “ancestors done, descendants ” hint verify, finding restate (recompute-don’t-inherit discipline Learning 65, applied feature rather inventory). what: Learning 73 — TDD on an intentional behavior change with exact-set characterization fixtures: derive the new expected sets from an INDEPENDENT read-only reference computation + per-delta justification (never from running the production change), and back them with from-first-principles driving tests that fail on the old code for the RIGHT reason (S74, implement #31 — gestation-derived dam-exclusion window)
title: nprcgenekeepr — Project-Specific Learnings
text: () [RED chicken--egg exact-set fixtures, resolved independent oracle + per-delta justification] behavior change rewrites expected output expect_identical characterization fixture (dams_1/dams_4), write new expected values running -yet-written production change — circular (asserting code matches ). Lesson: new expected values characterization-fixture behavior change come independent derivation (reference computation can read, plus per-row “changed” check), production code test — comment block recording delta’s justification turns “silently regenerated” “recomputed justified” (umbrella’s explicit bar). (b) [characterization fixtures lock surface; CORRECTNESS proof separate, -first-principles driving tests] exact-set fixtures regression net, proof rule. added two tests prove rule independently rhesus fixture’s accidents: (1) hand-verifiable synthetic pedigree — focal animal plus DAM_IN (another offspring +200 d) DAM_OUT (+400 d) — asserting DAM_IN excluded maxGestationalPeriod=210 retained 180, isolating exact window edge values verifiable hand; (2) differential/responsiveness test asserting BRI2MW’s dam set differs 165 d 210 d (acceptance criterion #2: selection must respond parameter, hard-coded half-year). fail shipped code right reason — synthetic one shipped uses fixed ±182.5 d window, differential one shipped dam selection ignored maxGestationalPeriod entirely. what: Learning 87 — Fixing a “noisy warning” bug under strict TDD: REPRODUCE firsthand FIRST to establish it is noise-not-data-loss (which decides the whole fix shape); suppress it SURGICALLY with withCallingHandlers + message-matched invokeRestart("muffleWarning") (never blanket suppressWarnings), and prove the surgery with teeth that an UNRELATED warning still propagates; consolidate across all readers via a shared @noRd internal helper (the package’s non-exported convention → document() no-op); and test a server-internal closure structurally while putting behavioral teeth on the exported readers (S89, fix #4 — “incomplete final line found by readTableHeader” on files with no trailing newline)

what: Learning 91 — Before running OR proposing a recurring-shaped task (audit / sweep / inventory), CHECK THE PROJECT’S OWN PROCESS-HISTORY ARTIFACTS AT SCOPING TIME — CHANGELOG.md, docs/audits/, and the recent SESSION_NOTES.md handoffs are cheap and authoritative and tell you whether it was just done: a recurring audit is a DIFF against the last baseline, not a full re-run. S95 ran a full 14-agent / ~483k-token sweep classifying all 14 open issues for “implemented-but-open” when S62 (docs/audits/BACKLOG_STALENESS_AUDIT_2026-06-12.md, 4 days prior) had already classified all 21 then-open issues with the identical question, AND the CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] entries (S89/S90/S92) + the S94 handoff already documented the implemented-but-open backlog being drained issue-by-issue (#4/#33/#49). The overlap surfaced only MID-EXECUTION (agents cited S62) and at report-writing (looking up the audits-dir naming convention) — never at scoping. The owner flagged it twice (“why was this in the backlog if already done?”, “you should have been able to check changelog also”). what: Learning 94 — Re-merging the long-lived add-methodology branch into master (the standing branch model): the safety check is NOT the ahead/behind count — prior PRs merged via MERGE COMMITS, so those merge-commit nodes show up as “master-only” commits and make master look “N ahead” when it has ZERO unique content. Verify a re-merge with a THREE-part recipe instead: (1) git merge-tree --write-tree origin/master origin/add-methodology → exit 0 = no conflicts; (2) git log origin/add-methodology..origin/master --oneline → confirm the only master-only commits are Merge pull request #NN nodes (add-methodology’s own work merged back), NOT independent work; (3) confirm master is strictly behind — comm -23 <(git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/master|sort) <(... add-methodology|sort) is empty (no master-only files) AND the tip-to-tip diff is an exact mirror (master-vs-add-methodology = the inverse of add-methodology-vs-master). All three held for PR #51 (S52–S99, 54 commits, +6001/−406, clean): merge-tree exit 0, the 2 master-only commits were Merge pull request #43/#41, no master-only files, mirror diff. (S100, PR #51 add-methodology → master)
title: nprcgenekeepr — Project-Specific Learnings

Reading number “master work ’d regress” trap. (1) decisive safety signal merge-tree + content subsumption, commit count. merge-tree’s clean exit proves 3-way merge applies conflicts; clean 3-way merge preserves master’s content unless add-methodology explicitly reverted lines (surface conflict). Pair mirror-diff / -master--files check prove master strictly behind (zero unique content), merge provably safe purely additive. (2) repo’s standing model, recurs — Learning 91’s “cite prior run” corollary applies branch topology . branch model “work add-methodology; master gets via PR” (S51 = PR #41, S52-ish = PR #43, S100 = PR #51). future add-methodology → master PR show growing “master ahead K merge-commits” divergence; next session expect run three-part recipe rather re-discovering divergence benign. (3) Right-size SOLO even ultracode (call S96/S99 pushes). PR one gh pr create pre-flight investigation; investigation handful deterministic git/gh reads, adversarial check matters (merge cleanly / lose anything?) answered merge-tree + mirror-diff, done inline. PR body published world; per SAFEGUARDS’ outward-facing caution, draft title/body, ground user-facing summary canonical NEWS.md/CHANGELOG.md (memory commits), confirm via AskUserQuestion creating — leave OPEN (merging master separate owner decision). what: Learning 95 — Before planning a CRAN “update/submission,” VERIFY THE PACKAGE’S ACTUAL CRAN STATUS FIRSTHAND (it may be ARCHIVED, which reshapes the whole submission path), and treat a clean one-time local R CMD check as necessary-but-NOT-sufficient — CRAN’s PERIODIC re-checks (not the submission check) archive established packages for timing/policy drift, so the deliverable is “fast/clean under --as-cran on an ongoing basis,” not “passed once.” nprcgenekeepr reads in CLAUDE.md and the repo as an established CRAN package (8 dated cran-comments.md, a CRAN-SUBMISSION marker, revdep/), and the owner framed the task as a routine “version bump + NEWS rewrite.” A firsthand WebFetch of cran.r-project.org/web/packages/nprcgenekeepr/index.html proved otherwise: “Archived on 2025-07-29 as issues were not corrected in time” — and the Archive dir + R-pkg-devel thread showed it had a 1.0.8 publish (2025-07-26) RE-archived ~3 days later over tested elapsed times, plus a prior 2022-11-03 archive/2025-04-24 unarchive cycle. (S101, CRAN 2.0.0 submission plan)

what: Learning 98 — A “should we adopt technology X to future-proof?” decision splits into THREE independent questions — (1) is the incumbent actually dying? (2) what does X concretely buy ON OUR constrained surface? (3) what does X cost there? — and the answer is frequently HYBRID (adopt X where it’s unconstrained and free; stay on the incumbent where the constraint lives), not all-or-nothing. Verify every external-ecosystem claim by adversarial web research, never from model memory. (S104, Quarto-vs-R-Markdown documentation future-proofing analysis — docs/planning/quarto-documentation-future-proofing-analysis.md)
title: nprcgenekeepr — Project-Specific Learnings

(3) X cost ? — Quarto vignette adds SystemRequirements Quarto-CLI dependency CRAN’s check machines DON’T guarantee (confirmed missing macOS flavors 2025), documented transient “vignettes” NOTE — bad trade already-archived package. Quarto maintainer (cderv) “advise” Quarto vignette engine CRAN vignettes. hybrid answer usually right one, ’s real “yes X,” dodge. Recommendation: keep CRAN vignettes knitr/rmarkdown (zero CRAN risk, officially supported indefinitely) adopting Quarto unconstrained surface pays carries CRAN dependency — pkgdown site, new long-form docs, slide decks, inst/extdata/ dev docs (two already .qmd). enabled fact, wish: pkgdown supports MIXED .qmd/.Rmd (since 2.1.0, 2024-07) via project: render: ['*.qmd']. one genuine strategic fork worth surfacing owner (deciding ): long-form manual CRAN vignette doc rewards Quarto — repositioned CRAN vignette set onto website. what: Learning 100 — Converting a doc Rmd → Quarto .qmd is not just a rename: (a) the target format has SEMANTIC differences the source didn’t (Quarto treats ::: as fenced-div/callout syntax; R Markdown doesn’t), so you must RENDER to catch them — a static rename hides them; (b) verify the conversion changes no package contents by applying the .Rbuildignore regexes to BOTH filenames, don’t assume “it was ignored so the new one is too”; (c) when the doc isn’t reproducibly renderable (dead hardcoded paths, unmaterialized packages), render with --no-execute to verify FORMAT validity and STATE the execution limitation — do not fake a full render, and do NOT “fix” the doc into being executable (that’s a behavior change, not a format conversion); (d) preserve the author’s historical prose byte-for-byte rather than rewrite it to silence a cosmetic warning whose output is verified correct (FM #22). (S106, Quarto Hybrid §7.1 slice 1 — inst/extdata/meeting_notes.Rmd → .qmd)

what: Learning 123 — To rewrite a large doc section deterministically, write the new section to a FILE and SPLICE it in by heading boundaries with R (read lines, find the start heading + the next heading, recombine head/new/tail) — far more robust than a fragile multi-hundred-line Edit match. For a NEWS rewrite: bind RED to the rendered NEWS.md; fold the user-facing delta from the per-session CHANGELOG/handoffs (DROP internal/test/VCS sessions); then adversarially verify completeness (vs git show HEAD:NEWS.md + the plan’s classification), accuracy (every named function exists/exported), and dedup/style BEFORE tightening prose. rmarkdown::render(output_format="github_document") drops an untracked NEWS.html preview — clean it before commit. (S130, owner pick B — CRAN Phase 3a, the NEWS 2.0.0 rewrite)

what: Learning 124 — For a version bump / metadata change with NO new behavior, do strict TDD by binding RED to the version-consistency invariant (every version-bearing artifact == target; stale strings absent), not to a function’s behavior. A version retitle in one file leaves dangling cross-references in other docs — sweep for them. (S131, owner pick B-cont — CRAN Phase 3b, the 2.0.0 version bump)

what: Learning 126 — A plan’s named root cause is a hypothesis: measure before fixing. what: Learning 129 — A firsthand-verified remote-state claim still has a shelf life: a branch can be pushed or changed between sessions, so a prior session’s correct “push first / N commits behind” snapshot can be stale by the time you act on it. git status “up to date with origin/” compares only against the LOCAL tracking ref, which updates only on fetch — so it reads “up to date” both when you already pushed and when your view of the remote is merely stale. Run git fetch THEN git rev-list --left-right --count origin/<branch>...HEAD to get ground truth before acting on an inherited “push first” prerequisite. (S136, owner pick Phase5-finish scope “prep + hand off” — CRAN Phase 5 local prep)

what: Learning 132 — A spell/lint flag on a GENERATED file can be a render-time artifact, not a source defect: pandoc’s smart-quotes turn straight '...' in an .Rmd into curly '...' in the .md, and a quote sitting against a word ('row.names' → names') becomes a bogus token. Fix it at the SOURCE in a way the renderer can’t undo — a code span (backticks) bypasses smart-quotes — then RE-RENDER and confirm the regenerated-file diff is confined to the one intended line. Never hand-edit the generated .md. (S139, owner directive — clear S138’s punch-list)

what: Learning 133 — Before merging a PR, triage its CI checks: a red check is not automatically a merge-blocker. gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus distinguishes BLOCKED (a required check is failing — do not merge) from UNSTABLE (mergeable; only non-required checks are red). When a check is red, read its log and CLASSIFY it — required vs optional, correctness vs style, introduced-by-this-PR vs pre-existing — and report that classification; don’t merge blind, and don’t refuse a merge the owner directed just because a non-required style check is red. (S140, owner directive “merge #54”)

what: Learning 134 — Clearing a lint check is a FIXPOINT problem, not a one-pass edit: an autofix that satisfies its TARGET linter can TRIGGER other linters (a cascade), so the only reliable completion signal is re-running lint_package() over the WHOLE tree after the per-file fixes and repeating until 0 — never trust a per-file fixer’s “done.” And a linter message is a suggestion, not a mandate: nonportable_path_linter fires on any /-bearing string (incl. MIME types), coalesce_linter assumes %||% exists — when the literal fix is wrong or unavailable, prefer # nolint (extending the author’s intent) or disabling the linter in .lintr, not the transformation the message names. (S141, owner pick — Lint cleanup → green CI; this clears the exact state Learning 133 flagged)

what: Learning 135 — To make a CI check’s fix demonstrably green you may have to MERGE it where the workflow runs: a check whose workflow triggers only on pull_request / push-to-default is invisible on a feature-branch push, so the fix’s green status is unverifiable until a PR runs — open the PR, watch all checks, then merge (do not merge blind). And when adopting a default-branch workflow, the local default branch is often badly STALE and git pull may be reconfigured to rebase (pull.rebase=true) — which a standing junk modification (.DS_Store) will block; sync a stale-but-ancestor local branch with git fetch + git reset --hard origin/<branch> (after git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/<branch> proves it’s an ff), NOT git pull. (S142, owner directive “work on 1, 2, and 3” + branch plan “merge now, switch to master”)

what: Learning 144 — To WIRE a new provider/capability to a caller, prefer adding a clean SYMMETRIC SIBLING over parameterizing a domain-named function: a new wrapper costs one export but has zero blast radius on existing signatures and avoids a naming smell (a LabKey-named function that also reads files); the “but a user can already compose it” critique is answered by PARITY — the sibling gives the new source the same first-class entry point the old source already has (the existing function is itself just a thin fetch→delegate wrapper). And a wrapper inherits its source’s contract, so do NOT copy a guard that can’t fire (no NULL guard on a loud-erroring source = no untested dead code). (S151, owner “publish + delete + wire the file provider”)

what: Learning 146 — After gh pr merge, the git fetch that precedes git reset --hard origin/<branch> MUST be verified to have SUCCEEDED before resetting — a transient network/DNS failure leaves the local origin/<branch> ref STALE, and reset --hard origin/<branch> then resets to the OLD pre-merge commit without any error, silently leaving the local branch BEHIND the real remote. Gate the reset on a post-fetch assertion that the just-merged commit is now an ancestor of origin/<branch>. (S153, publish S152 — focal-file source merge)
title: nprcgenekeepr — Project-Specific Learnings

Publishing S152: pushed wire-focal-file-source, opened PR #63, watched CI 10/10, confirmed CLEAN/MERGEABLE, gh pr merge 63 --merge → merge commit e1780c02 (verified state: MERGED firsthand). standard reconcile (Learning 135: fetch+reset, pull). ran post-merge git fetch git reset --hard origin/master command block — fetch hit transient resolve host: github.com. fetch failed, local origin/master stayed STALE pre-merge cb46616e, git reset --hard origin/master happily reset local master OLD commit, exit 0, error. reason caught : block also asserted “merged commit 4f362be9 ancestor origin/master?” printed — impossible right confirmed merge, ref stale. Recovered: retried git fetch loop (succeeded attempt 1) → origin/master advanced cb46616e..e1780c02; re-asserted 4f362be9 now ancestor (YES); git reset --hard origin/master → local master = e1780c02; confirmed R/getFocalAnimalPedFromFile.R + R/readFocalAnimalIds.R present. trap: git reset --hard origin/<branch> operates whatever LOCAL remote-tracking ref currently — failed/skipped fetch makes -op--stale, error, “exit 0” evidence reconcile worked. Reflexes: [never chain git fetch git reset --hard origin/<branch> fetch can’t fail — verify fetch SUCCEEDED (exit status / old..new ref update line) resetting][gh pr merge, assert merged commit ancestor origin/<branch> (git merge-base ---ancestor <mergedSHA> origin/<branch>) reset — post-merge means stale ref, missing merge][retry transient git fetch (DNS / resolve host) short loop rather treating first failure terminal][treat “exit 0” git reset --hard origin/<branch> necessary--sufficient — confirm git rev-parse origin/<branch> actually advanced expected SHA]. Apply: every post-merge local reconcile; reset --hard origin/<branch> depends just-run fetch; sandboxed/flaky-network sessions git fetch can fail transiently.

what: Learning 147 — To enrich a fail-soft boundary that swallows WHY into a bare NULL, return a DEDICATED classed error carrying the reason (do NOT overload the shared error/QC object with a different concern); wrap EVERY read the boundary performs (a read left outside the tryCatch is a latent UNCAUGHT throw, not fail-soft); MAP low-level stop() text to clean user-facing messages rather than leaking an internal fnName(): ... prefix; and treat a “silent empty” result (0-row / opaque NULL) as its own reported failure. (S155, richer offline-focal error messages)

what: Learning 149 – After ANY renv bump / self-upgrade, run a fresh-R-startup smoke test (Phase 3E): an renv self-upgrade can leave renv/activate.R with an UNSUBSTITUTED ..md5.. template placeholder, which throws object '..md5..' not found the moment .Rprofile sources it – breaking every R session started in the project. The lockfile looks correct and a check that does not cold-start R in the project root will not catch it. Fix by regenerating with the installed renv (renv::activate()), which fills in the md5; then re-source to confirm. (S157, commit the renv 1.1.4->1.2.3 bump)

text: happened. FAILED: object '..md5..' found, halted, source("renv/activate.R") (called .Rprofile). Diagnosis: line 6 new activate.R attr(version, "md5") <- ..md5.. – literal ..md5.. template token, never substituted (sibling version <- "1.2.3" substituted; md5 placeholder leaked). Confirmed REGRESSION, pre-existing: old 1.1.4 activate.R sourced cleanly --vanilla (warning installed!=recorded renv, mismatch bump meant fix); new one threw ..md5... renv 1.2.3 installed system library, regenerated via Rscript --vanilla -e 'renv::activate(project=getwd())' (.Rprofile, broken file auto-sourced; restore/snapshot side effects – activate.R changed, renv.lock untouched). Line 6 became attr(version, "md5") <- "1bd9f58e..." fresh .Rprofile startup printed “renv: 1.2.3 – startup OK”. broken activate.R lived local-unpushed commit, --amended away (renv.lock half already correct; activate.R needed md5). Net: broken artifact never entered shared history. what: Learning 150 – When a duplicate-config-file precedence bug is the diagnosis, the fix is exactly ONE file (eliminate the precedence question entirely) – and you can verify the fix AT THE CONFIG LAYER this session rather than deferring to “the next PR”: codecov exposes https://codecov.io/validate, which echoes the PARSED config (so you see the actual thresholds it will apply); POST a SECRET-REDACTED copy so no committed token leaves the machine. Do the complete job (remove the now-dead .Rbuildignore entry for the deleted file), and PRESERVE – do not silently strip – an embedded credential you happen to be rewriting (rotation is a separate owner decision; FM #8). what: Learning 151 – To silence a benign warning that a fail-soft boundary’s underlying read emits BEFORE the error that gets caught, add a TARGETED warning muffler at the READ SITE (withCallingHandlers + invokeRestart("muffleWarning") matched to the specific message) – do NOT broaden the shared muffler (widens blast radius across all its callers) and do NOT pre-check file.exists() (that changes a SHARED helper’s THROWN error and misses the exists-but-unreadable case). The muffle is control-flow-neutral: the error still propagates, so the caught classed result is unchanged – assert BOTH “no warning” AND “error still thrown”. (S159, quiet the offline focal-id read’s read.csv “cannot open file” warning)

what: Learning 153 – To DOCUMENT/EXPOSE an already-exported-but-undocumented function, the right artifact is a WEBSITE-ONLY Quarto article in the existing scripting series (vignettes/articles/*.qmd, which is .Rbuildignored) – NOT a NEWS line, and NOT a shipped CRAN vignette unless the owner asks. Copy a sibling article’s EXACT shape (genetic-value-analysis.qmd: YAML title:-only, a hidden setup chunk knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>"), ## X {#sec-x} sections, then Key arguments + See also + References), and ALSO add the function to inst/_pkgdown.yml’s reference list(s) so pkgdown does not warn “topic missing from index”. Verify the EXECUTABLE doc in two steps: (1) run every intended chunk in-session under pkgload::load_all to confirm REAL outputs BEFORE writing prose; (2) render via quarto render <file>.qmd as the doc build-equivalent, then REMOVE the render litter (.html, _files/, the quarto-created .gitignore, .quarto/) – only the .qmd is tracked. A website-only article earns a CHANGELOG entry but NO NEWS entry (NEWS is for SHIPPED package changes; S116 precedent + [[news-vs-changelog]]), which also sidesteps the NEWS smart-quote/en-dash render traps (132/139) – keep the .qmd pure ASCII regardless. (S161, document/expose the offline focal-animal workflow)

what: Learning 154 – When the deliverable is “make X CONSISTENT across a SET of parallel docs/files”, it is ONE coherent deliverable (single theme + single definition-of-done), NOT bundling – but only if the items genuinely share that theme; stitching unrelated small carryovers together IS bundling (FM #18/#25). Do it in this order: (1) build the actual coverage MATRIX first by firsthand reads (FROM->TO) so “consistent” is a measurable target, not a vibe; (2) MATCH the existing convention – do not redesign the mechanism (here: bold-title prose mentions, not hyperlinks; switching to links would be a separate out-of-scope mode switch); (3) pick a single canonical order + a per-item description policy so consistency is verifiable, not just asserted; (4) verify completeness with a GREP over the matrix, not by eyeballing; (5) the build-equivalent is proportionate to WHAT CHANGED – a prose-only edit needs the markdown->HTML render to pass, not a re-derivation of unchanged simulation outputs. (S162, cross-link the five vignettes/articles/*.qmd scripting articles)

what: Learning 155 – A recurring render-time artifact that a standing gotcha tells you to “work around on every render” should be eliminated at the RENDERER-CONFIG SOURCE so the workaround is never needed again – this turns a standing gotcha into a CLOSED one. Here two NEWS render traps that S139/S147 had been hand-mitigating every time were fixed permanently with two NEWS.Rmd github_document knobs: html_preview: false (no top-level NEWS.html byproduct -> no “non-standard file at top level” R CMD check NOTE; Learning 139) and md_extensions: "-smart" (pandoc’s smart extension OFF -> source -- and straight quotes render to ASCII --/" instead of en-dash/curly; Learning 132). Three execution rules that made it clean: (1) VERIFY both knobs on throwaway /tmp Rmds BEFORE touching anything tracked – prove -smart yields ASCII output and html_preview:false suppresses the .html; you then present a verified plan, not a hypothesis. (2) Smart-off fixes FUTURE renders, but pre-existing LITERAL curly quotes baked into the SOURCE survive a re-render – find them with grep -nP '[^\x00-\x7F]' on the .Rmd (here NEWS.Rmd:189/:213) and fix each at the source. (3) When re-rendering to clean historical bytes, prove the regenerated file is CONTENT-INVARIANT by normalizing the OLD file’s smart-bytes back to ASCII (perl -CSD -pe 's/\x{201C}|\x{201D}/"/g; s/\x{2018}|\x{2019}/\x27/g; s/\x{2013}/--/g; s/\x{2014}/---/g; s/\x{2026}/.../g') and diffing vs the new render – the residual should be EMPTY or only a benign SOFT-WRAP shift (an en-dash is 1 column, -- is 2, so a line near pandoc’s ~79-col wrap can break one word later – same words, different newline; NOT a content change). The NEWS-encoding change earns a CHANGELOG entry, NOT a NEWS line (NEWS infrastructure is not a user-facing package change; [[news-vs-changelog]]). (S163, permanent NEWS render fix)

what: Learning 156 – When “make X a FIRST-CLASS column/field” lands in a pipeline that ALREADY retains unknown inputs (here qcStudbook() keeps any unrecognized header as a trailing novelCol via intersect(getPossibleCols(), cols) then c(cols, novelCols)), the discriminator between first-class and retained-but-orphaned is CANONICAL ORDER + DECLARED TYPE, never mere presence – so the RED tests must assert PLACEMENT (the new column sorts into its registry position, e.g. immediately after sex) and TYPE-COERCION (a factor input becomes character), because “is in the output” and “is character (from a CSV read)” already pass for a novelCol and would be false-GREEN. The minimal GREEN was two edits: add "species" to getPossibleCols() (which alone fixes presence + ordering, since the intersect orders by the registry) and one if (any("species" %in% cols)) sb$species <- as.character(sb$species) beside the sibling optional-column conversions (which fixes the factor case). (S165, issue #46 item 1 – species as a first-class column)

what: Learning 157 – Two sharpenings of the publish convention from publishing a user-facing CODE change (vs the recent NEWS-infra-only publishes). (a) NEWS-vs-CHANGELOG for the CHANGE TYPE, not the session: when the session being published shipped a real user-facing package change (here a newly recognized + typed pedigree column) and the prior session deliberately DEFERRED the NEWS line as “a pre-publish decision”, the publish session’s FIRST step is to resolve it – per [[news-vs-changelog]] a user-facing code change earns a NEWS entry (not CHANGELOG-only like the S155/S163/S164 NEWS-infra publishes) – add the bullet to NEWS.Rmd, re-render to NEWS.md with the permanent html_preview:false+md_extensions:"-smart" config (Learning 155; verify grep -cP '[^\x00-\x7F]' NEWS.md -> 0 and the diff is a confined pure-insertion), and COMMIT it on the feature branch so it ships WITH the feature in the same PR (one PR, not a follow-up). (b) A long gh pr checks <n> --watch is NOT a reliable terminal signal: it can die mid-run on a transient HTTP 401: Requires authentication and exit NON-zero, AND the harness background-completion notification can report “exit code 0” while the captured $? was 1 – a disagreement that can read as “all green” when ~half the matrix was still pending. Defensive “don’t merge blind”: never trust the watch’s exit; after it returns, re-query FRESH with a non-watch gh pr checks <n> and confirm EVERY check is pass with overall exit 0 (gh returns 8 while any check is pending) before the merge. (S166, publish S165 – PR #68, issue #46 item 1)

what: Learning 158 – When a per-key feature ships a lookup table whose only seeded value EQUALS the fallback default (here speciesGestation = one row, rhesus -> 210, with a 210 fallback), the feature is a no-op on shipped data, so a CONSUMER-level test cannot observe key differentiation and an “ignores the key, always uses the default” bug would pass GREEN – the consumer-boundary corollary of Learning 156 (test the discriminator, not presence). The fix that keeps the owner’s single-row table AND makes per-key behavior genuinely testable is to add a table-INJECTION parameter at the consumer boundary (getPotentialParents(..., gestationTable = NULL), threaded to getSpeciesGestation) so a RED test can inject a multi-row fixture with DISTINCT values plus a mixed-key fixture and assert the per-key path changes the output (here a RHESUS=210 vs TESTSP=90 mixed-species pedigree where one shared candidate dam is excluded for the 210 focal but retained for the 90 focal – a single fixed window cannot satisfy both). Two operational corollaries on consuming a NEW data/ object from a package function: (a) reference it by bare name and add utils::globalVariables("<obj>") to suppress the “no visible binding for global variable” R CMD check NOTE (precedent R/modSummaryStats.R:4); (b) lintr’s object_usage_linter resolves globals against the INSTALLED namespace, so a NEW exported function or NEW data object referenced across files throws a FALSE “no visible global function/binding” lint until you devtools::install(quick = TRUE) – re-install before trusting single-file lint, then the warnings clear. (S167, issue #46 item 2 – species-keyed gestation period)

what: Learning 159 – A prior handoff’s prescribed fix can carry a wrong MECHANISM; verify the fix PATH exists before following it. The S167 handoff (and its CHANGELOG/Learning 158) said the pre-existing R CMD check spelling NOTE (“untyped” in NEWS.md) should be cleared by “adding to inst/WORDLIST AND regenerating tests/spelling.Rout.save” – but tests/spelling.Rout.save DOES NOT EXIST in this package. The spelling check is spelling::spell_check_test(vignettes = TRUE, error = FALSE, skip_on_cran = TRUE) (tests/spelling.R) backed by inst/WORDLIST as the whitelist; the WORDLIST is the ONLY lever – there is no .Rout.save to regenerate. Adding the bare word “untyped” to inst/WORDLIST took the local fast R CMD check (--as-cran, no vignettes/manual) from 1 NOTE -> 0/0/0, confirming both the NOTE’s source and the fix in one run. Second, empirically grounded: spelling::spell_check_package(".") SKIPS markdown code spans (backtick-delimited inline code), so backticked identifiers are never checked and need no WORDLIST entry – only bare PROSE words are. Proof: two new NEWS bullets dense with NEW backticked identifiers (getSpeciesGestation, speciesGestation) plus prose (“macaque”, “whitespace”, “lookup”, “extensible”, “seeded”) added ZERO new flagged words; the only unrecognized word stayed “untyped” (S166’s bare-prose term, which sits outside backticks). So a user-facing NEWS edit normally needs no WORDLIST change as long as code is backticked and prose stays dictionary-clean – but RUN spell_check_package to KNOW the exact delta rather than predicting which words trip. what: Learning 160 – A Shiny reactive PREFILL (“default this input from loaded data, but let the user override”) has a testServer trap and a clobber trap; both are solved by moving the logic OUT of the side-effect. Trap 1 (testServer): in shiny::testServer (MockShinySession) an update*Input() call does NOT echo back into input$<id> – there is no browser round-trip – so input$maxGestationalPeriod stays whatever session$setInputs() last made it, and a test that “sets a pedigree, then reads the input to see the prefill” can NEVER observe the update; it is a structurally false test. Fix: do not assert the updateNumericInput side-effect. Factor the computation that matters into PURE helpers (firstPedigreeSpecies(ped) -> first non-NA/non-empty species or NA_character_; pedigreeGestationDefault(ped, gestationTable=NULL) = getSpeciesGestation(firstPedigreeSpecies(ped), gestationTable)) and expose the computed default as a reactive in the module’s returned list (gestationDefault), so testServer asserts session$getReturned()$gestationDefault() directly while the observer merely drives the (untested-by-assertion, exercised-for-coverage) side-effect. The shipped-table-collapses-to-default false-GREEN (Learning 158) recurs here too: bundled speciesGestation maps every species to 210, so differentiation is proven only with an INJECTED gestationTable (RHESUS=210 vs TESTSP=90) threaded through a new optional module param. Trap 2 (clobber / re-fire): the documented “dragon” – an unguarded observeEvent(data(), update*Input(...)) (precedent modBreedingGroups.R:429, which resets viewGrp to 1 every time groups reform) overwrites a user’s manual edit whenever the data reactive re-invalidates. Guard with a reactiveVal sentinel holding the last value the module wrote (lastAutoSet <- reactiveVal(<UI initial>)) and a pure decision helper prefillGuardAllows(current, lastAuto) = TRUE iff current is NULL/NA or == lastAuto (i.e. the user has NOT edited away from what we set); prefill + record lastAutoSet(newDefault) only when it returns TRUE. Critically, the observer keys on the DATA reactive (pedigree()), never on the input it writes, so the updateNumericInput -> input$ change does not re-trigger it (no loop). Architecture choice at the pre-RED gate: keep the STATIC UI numericInput + a server observer over a server-rendered uiOutput/renderUI – smaller blast radius, the existing value="210" UI test stays green, and adding a reactive to the returned list is safe because the existing list test uses %in% (subset), not identity. (S169, issue #46 item 2b – species-keyed UI prefill of the gestation window)

what: Learning 161 – The local fast R CMD check is NOT apples-to-apples with the PR CI matrix, and its extra WARNINGs/NOTE can be artifacts of the LOCAL tree + build flags rather than publishable-tree defects – prove each is outside the git tree before chasing it, and treat PR CI (which checks out the git tree on 5 platforms and builds vignettes) as the authoritative gate. Three concrete sources seen this session, none a real defect: (a) an untracked stray file with a non-portable name trips “checking for portable file names” – R CMD build sweeps in UNTRACKED files from the package dir, so a macOS/cloud-sync duplicate like tests/testthat/test_species_first_class 2.R (the ” 2” suffix, a space -> non-portable) lands in the tarball and WARNs locally, yet it is not in git so CI never sees it; ISOLATE by moving it aside (mv to /tmp) and re-running the check (WARNING -> OK confirms it was the sole delta), then restore it as-found (do not delete an uncommitted file without owner say-so, SAFEGUARDS); (b) --no-build-vignettes leaves inst/doc empty -> two spurious vignette WARNINGs (“Files in the ‘vignettes’ directory but no files in ‘inst/doc’” + “Directory ‘inst/doc’ does not exist”) – CI builds vignettes so they do not appear there; for a clean local read use devtools::check(vignettes = FALSE) (suppresses the inst/doc check) or actually build vignettes; (c) --as-cran incoming-feasibility yields the STANDING archived-on-CRAN NOTE (“Package was archived on CRAN”, “New submission”) whenever the check reaches the network – permanent since 2025-07-29, not a finding. Net: a docs-only publish that returns “3 WARNINGs + 1 NOTE” locally can still be 0 publishable-tree findings; the proof is PR CI passing clean on the merge-result tree. (S170, publish S169 – PR #70, issue #46 item 2b)

what: Learning 162 – Renaming an EXPORTED package function is a public-API change: the safe, owner-approved shape is “add the new canonical name, keep the OLD name as a thin DEPRECATED alias” (both @exported), NOT a hard rename – the old name’s body becomes { .Deprecated("<new>"); <new>(args) }. .Deprecated() infers the OLD name from the call stack and builds a message naming the NEW one, so the RED test pins the deprecation by matching the NEW name: expect_warning(oldName(x), "newName") plus expect_identical(oldName(x), newName(x)) for behaviour-preservation; the new name’s own behaviour test (expect_identical(newName(3L), list(1L,2L,3L))) fails RED with “could not find function” until GREEN. Three rename-specific reflexes verified this session: (a) git grep IS the exhaustive inventory – it lists every tracked reference deterministically, so SPLIT the hits into must-change CODE (the def file via git mv, the in-package callers, roxygen @examples, the test call, NAMESPACE/man/ regenerated by document(), and the inst/_pkgdown.yml reference index – list BOTH names there since both stay exported+documented or pkgdown warns “missing topics”) vs DO-NOT-TOUCH history (SESSION_NOTES.md, *-cran-comments.md, docs/audits/*, TECH_DEBT_* describe the PAST state; rewriting them is scope creep). (b) A newly-added cross-file function throws a FALSE object_usage_linter “no visible global function definition for ‘’” in single-file lintr::lint() AND lint_package() until the package namespace knows it – object_usage resolves globals against the INSTALLED/loadable namespace, so the new symbol looks undefined while the sibling already-installed call (makeGroupMembers) resolves fine; pkgload::load_all() then re-lint -> 0, and CI installs before linting so it never fires there. Same root cause as Learning 158b (a NEW EXPORTED symbol -> false object_usage until install(quick = TRUE)); here load_all() suffices and devtools::check() does not run lintr at all. (c) A function NAME that lands in man-page PROSE (the alias page \title{Deprecated alias for makeGroupNum}) trips spell_check_package because titles are prose, NOT the \name/\alias/\usage/\code contexts the checker skips – the lever is inst/WORDLIST (matching the already-present grpNum, which is in a title for the same reason; insert in C-locale sort position) OR wrap the identifier in \code{}; verified 0-unrecognized after adding makeGroupNum. Build-equivalent devtools::check(vignettes = FALSE) (Learning 161) = 0/0/0 confirmed the whole rename clean; the new deprecation warning is captured by the alias’s expect_warning and does NOT leak into the suite’s warning count (confirmed by isolating warning sources to the pre-existing test_modPyramid.R baseline). (S171, issue #29 – rename makeGrpNum -> makeGroupNum)

what: Learning 164 – The Genetic Value Analysis has TWO independent rank paths fed by ONE upstream value, and the Shiny-displayed rank is NOT the library orderReport rank. reportGV computes indivMeanKin <- meanKinship(kmat) (R/reportGV.R:93) – the single choke point – then path (A) orderReport/rankSubjects (R/reportGV.R:150, R/orderReport.R:27-85) buckets + ranks for the library report, while path (B) the Shiny module OVERWRITES that rank with rank(report$indivMeanKin - report$gu) (R/modGeneticValue.R:204-206) for the table users actually see. CONSEQUENCE for any GVA-ranking change: fix at the choke point (the shared indivMeanKin) to move BOTH paths; a fix only in orderReport is invisible in the app. Verified the issue-#9 premise adversarially (real qcPed: top-20 GVA ranks are 100% founders, mean kinship 0.0027-0.0035 vs colony 0.0066) – missing-parent animals become U-id founders (addUIds/addParents via qcStudbook.R:198-199), get self-kinship 0.5 + zero to all others (kinship.R:77-88), so low mean kinship + high genome uniqueness (own gene-drop alleles) => false top rank. The noParentage bucket (orderReport.R:46-47) protects ONLY is.na(origin) & totalOffspring==0 & founder and shipped under issue #8, not #9. Two blast-radius boundaries: kinship() has 5 R/ callers (reportGV.R:87, modBreedingGroups.R:173, modSummaryStats.R:357, createSimKinships.R:58, cumulateSimKinships.R:61) so a GVA-only fix must stay at the reportGV level, NOT in shared kinship(); and test_orderReport.R:24,42 hard-codes the buggy ranking (countUnk(top 100)==34), so a correct fix breaks it BY DESIGN – update intentionally. (S174, plan issue #9)

what: Learning 187 – A “fix EVERY stale X” deliverable’s completeness check must grep ALL tracked file extensions (use git grep with NO --include filter), because even a RATIFIED plan’s own evidence inventory can have a blind spot – and an adversarial completeness workflow catches multi-surface inconsistencies a single author misses. Implementing issue #2 Slice 3 (align the gene-drop default 5000 -> 1000L + reconcile every stale “5000” doc + the gvaConvergence() vignette). The plan’s mandated “84-hit 2D inventory” (the evidence grep that planning sessions are required to run) had omitted *.qmd, so a stale | guIter | 5000L | default claim in the tracked pkgdown article vignettes/articles/genetic-value-analysis.qmd:193 was NOT in the inventory – and my OWN first-pass grep repeated the omission (I used an explicit --include=*.R,*.Rmd,*.Rd,*.html,*.md,*.yml list). Four load-bearing techniques:

what: Learning 334 – A synthetic identical-proof for a cross-library file-format swap can pass cleanly while the real production data still breaks, because the divergence lives in a COLUMN TYPE the synthetic sample never included – run the actual exported caller against real data through the full build-equivalent before declaring the refactor’s proof complete, not just a hand-built toy example. (S363, fixing the Windows-only WriteXLS/create_wkbk() CI flakiness BACKLOG.md flagged S361/S362 – R-CMD-check.yaml red on windows-latest for 7+ consecutive sessions via a Perl-on-Windows WriteXLS::WriteXLS() dependency. Owner-directed via the Phase 0 priorities picker, then a second AskUserQuestion choosing the root-cause fix (replace WriteXLS with openxlsx) over the narrower test-guard option, then a third AskUserQuestion (TDD gate) approving REFACTOR-only per [[refactor-only]] – no new observable behavior, pure backend swap. REFACTOR-class, TDD RED/GREEN N/A.) (a) [the gate-time proof looked sufficient and wasn’t] Before touching R/create_wkbk.R, this session captured a pre-change reference (return value + per-sheet readxl::read_excel() content, including an NA cell) from the CURRENT WriteXLS-based implementation, then proved the post-swap openxlsx-based output byte-for-byte identical() against it – return value TRUE, sheet names, column names, row counts, and values all matched exactly. devtools::test_file() on both directly-affected test files (test_create_wkbk.R, test_readKinshipOverrides.R) passed unchanged. Every check available at that point said the refactor was behavior-preserving. (b) [the full build-equivalent found what the narrower proof missed] Running devtools::check(args = "--as-cran") – the actual project build-equivalent, not a targeted test-file run – surfaced 2 failures in test_modInput_excelSireDam.R, a file this session had not touched and had no reason to suspect: session$getReturned()$cleanedStudbook() came back plain NULL instead of a data.frame. Direct reproduction (readExcelPOSIXToCharacter() on a freshly makeExamplePedigreeFile(fileType = "excel")-written file, then qcStudbook() on the result) isolated the mechanism precisely: as.Date.default() errored trying to parse the round-tripped birth/exit columns, which runQcStudbook()’s internal tryCatch silently absorbed into a “Data Processing Error” that set hasErrors <- TRUE and forced cleaned <- NULL – no crash surfaced to the caller, just a quietly empty result. (c) [isolating the actual byte-level divergence, not just the symptom] Writing the SAME examplePedigree data through WriteXLS::WriteXLS() directly (still installed locally, just no longer a package dependency) and through the new openxlsx path, then reading both back via the package’s own readExcelPOSIXToCharacter() (read_excel(col_types = "text")), showed the Date-class birth/exit columns diverging: the WriteXLS file’s text round-trip produced correctly formatted "1965-07-02" strings; the openxlsx file’s produced raw Excel serial numbers ("23925"). openxlsx::read.xlsx(..., detectDates = TRUE) confirmed the new file’s cells DID carry a genuine date-formatted numeric type (auto-applied by openxlsx::writeData()’s built-in Date-class detection) – and explicitly re-applying openxlsx::addStyle() with createStyle(numFmt = "yyyy-mm-dd") did not change the readxl text-mode result either. The conclusion, confirmed by elimination rather than assumed: readxl::read_excel(col_types = "text") returns a numeric-formatted cell’s raw STORED value as text regardless of its number format – it is not format-aware in text mode – so any cell holding a genuinely-typed date-as-number (however it got that way) round-trips to a serial number under this package’s own text-forced read path. WriteXLS’s Perl backend evidently wrote Date columns as literal text cells instead, which is why the OLD behavior “just worked” under the same reader. (d) [the fix embeds the actual required invariant, not a general dependency swap] create_wkbk() now explicitly detects Date/POSIXct columns per data.frame in df_list and coerces them to character (as.character()) BEFORE calling openxlsx::write.xlsx(), rather than relying on openxlsx’s “more correct” native date-cell typing – because this package’s OWN and ONLY read path for files create_wkbk() produces is the col_types = "text" reader, matching what WriteXLS apparently did all along. Re-running the full devtools::check() after the fix: 0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes; the specific previously-failing test (test_modInput_excelSireDam.R) passed; a strengthened synthetic identical-proof including an explicit Date column (with an NA) now matches WriteXLS’s reference output exactly. (e) [why this matters beyond this one fix] [[identical-proof]] says to prove a refactor byte-identical() against a captured reference – sound advice, but for a refactor that swaps the LIBRARY serializing a binary file format (not just an in-memory algorithm), byte-identical files are structurally unreachable, and a synthetic proof is only as strong as the column TYPES it happens to include. The synthetic df_list built to satisfy the TDD gate’s stated identical-proof requirement used only character/numeric columns – entirely reasonable-looking, and still missed the one type class (Date) that broke in production. The generalizable rule: for a cross-library file-format swap, run the actual EXPORTED caller against REAL representative data through the full build-equivalent (not a narrower test-file run, and not only a hand-built synthetic sample) before declaring the identical-proof complete – the synthetic proof is a useful first pass, not a substitute for exercising the real call graph. A new glossary entry, [[cross-library-file-format-proof]], generalizes this for future refactors of the same shape. Carried as applied: [[refactor-only]] (declared PRE-RED→REFACTOR via AskUserQuestion, no synthetic RED manufactured); [[identical-proof]] (attempted first, refined per (e) once it proved insufficient); [[regression-read]] (full test_dir(reporter="silent") clean read: 1 pre-existing unrelated failure isolated and NOT fixed, see Learning note below); [[consult-project-source-of-truth]] (installed openxlsx directly rather than assuming its date-handling behavior from memory, and empirically eliminated hypotheses – explicit numFmt style, writeData() vs write.xlsx() – rather than guessing at the mechanism).

what: Learning 668 – A “not verified” caveat removed from one document because a structural check now supports it does not transfer to a sibling document that received the identical caveat for what reads as the same problem – coverage has to be checked fixture-by-fixture against what each document actually claims, not document-by-document against the general defect class. (S636, 2026-08-25/26, implementing Track D of docs/planning/pedigree-diagram-kinship2-structural-comparison-plan.md.) vignettes/articles/kinship2-fidelity-validation.qmd and docs/planning/pedigree-diagram-kinship2-reference-comparison.qmd both received the identical S631 “diagram-equivalence claims are not currently verified” caveat in the same session (S631), for what reads as the same underlying gap. Track D’s own plan section 4.4 said, literally, to remove both caveats “only if [Track C’s comparator] supports it.” But the comparator (.comparePedigreeStructures(), run this session against the FIRST document’s own Track B/C fixtures – a 16-subject shrink fixture and a 9-subject consanguineous-dogleg fixture) provides zero evidence about the SECOND document’s claims, which rest on 4 completely different example pedigrees (sample.ped families 1/2, a 16-person genotyped case, a multi-mate “crowding” case) that were never run through that comparator or any other. Following the plan’s literal text would have removed a “not verified” warning from claims that remained exactly as unverified as before – citing evidence for a claim it never actually tested. Presented the gap explicitly via AskUserQuestion before acting, rather than resolving it either way unilaterally; owner chose to remove only the first document’s caveat (fully supported: 3/3 fixtures identical = TRUE) and add a one-paragraph note to the second document naming the untested gap by name, leaving its own caveat standing. Practical rule: when two documents share a caveat because they share a problem (not because they share the underlying data), a fix that resolves the problem for one is not evidence the problem is resolved for the other – trace what a given piece of verification evidence actually covers (which fixtures went through it, which specific claims it bears on) against what each document individually asserts, rather than treating “the defect class was addressed somewhere” as license to lift every caveat that named it.

text: markerObservedHeterozygosity computes, per animal, fraction genotyped loci heterozygous (Ho). markerExpectedHeterozygosity computes Nei’s (1973) gene diversity () locus population’s allele frequencies, plus unweighted mean across loci population-wide summary – standard observed-vs-expected heterozygosity diagnostic. take genotypeMatrix shape markerKinship. example uses three animals (X, Y, Z) genotyped 4 loci, Y missing call L4. Notice C2’s excluded column FALSE (tolerant test ) even though LOD -Inf: single opposite-homozygote locus (C2 B/B L1, O /) zero-tolerance Mendelian impossibility likelihood model, allowance ordinary genotyping error way exclusion count . delta C1 Inf, large finite number – gap -Inf-ranked neighbor reported infinite, design.

text: markerLdBlock takes different, classical view marker relationships: pairwise linkage disequilibrium (LD) loci sharing chromosome, using Hedrick’s (1987) frequency-weighted D’ multiallelic r² generalization, phase frequencies estimated EM algorithm (generalizing Excoffier & Slatkin 1995) since package’s genotype matrix unphased. explicitly secondary, exploratory statistic pair markerRealizedRelatednessVariance – classical LD theory assumes random mating, pedigreed colony violates, every row output carries fixed caveat saying . Note r² (1/3) move lockstep D’ – two statistics capture different aspects association, needn’t agree.

title: Forming Breeding Groups
text: Breeding-group formation needs two ingredients: list candidate animals kinship matrix giving relatedness every candidate every . derived quality-controlled pedigree. qcStudbook() validates standardizes studbook (checking parentage, sexes, dates, minimum parent age). Next mark focal population – , non-founders still colony (least one known parent) – trim pedigree animals plus ancestors needed compute kinships. reportGV() runs genetic value analysis – part need – returns kinship matrix trimmed pedigree. small guIter keeps article quick render. real analyses use guIter >= 1000; genome-uniqueness estimates stabilize many iterations. Finally, choose candidates – , animals born 2013 still colony.
code: breederPed <- qcStudbook(examplePedigree,   minSireAge    = 2.0,   minDamAge     = 2.0,   reportChanges = FALSE,   reportErrors  = FALSE ) focalAnimals <- breederPed$id[!(is.na(breederPed$sire) &   is.na(breederPed$dam)) &   is.na(breederPed$exit)] breederPed <- setPopulation(ped = breederPed, ids = focalAnimals) trimmedPed <- trimPedigree(focalAnimals, breederPed)  length(focalAnimals) #> [1] 327 dim(trimmedPed) #> [1] 704  14 trimmedGeneticValue <- reportGV(trimmedPed,   guIter   = 50, # genome-uniqueness iterations; use >= 1000 in practice   guThresh = 3,   byID     = TRUE,   updateProgress = NULL ) kmat <- trimmedGeneticValue[["kinship"]] dim(kmat) #> [1] 327 327 candidates <- trimmedPed$id[trimmedPed$birth < as.Date("2013-01-01") &   !is.na(trimmedPed$birth) &   is.na(trimmedPed$exit)] length(candidates) #> [1] 280

title: Validating the Founder-Genome-Equivalent Standard Error
text: Founder genome equivalents (FG, [Lacy 1989]) summarize much colony’s founding genetic diversity survives living population. Like genome uniqueness, FG estimated gene-drop simulation, carries Monte Carlo sampling noise shrinks number iterations grows. calcFGSE() reports noise standard error, FG can shown FG ± SE. Unlike genome uniqueness – simple average, whose standard error column variance – FG non-linear function random per-founder retention vector r: FG=(∑fpf2/rf)−1, FG = \left( \sum_f p_f^2 / r_f \right)^{-1}, standard error obtained delta method (first-order linearization), folding within-iteration covariance among founders. standard error derived way trustworthy calibrated – number reports must match real run--run spread FG. article recorded evidence , real deep pedigree, SE surfaced users. “validate expose” gate compute → validate → surface sequence.
